text: Supports standard protocols OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0, and SAML

quote: Documentation for the Adminstration RESTful API

text: Central admin console for managing all aspects of the server

quote: Through the account management console users can manage their own accounts. They can update the profile, change passwords, and setup two-factor authentication.

text: Single sign-on: log in once to access multiple registered applications
quote: Login once to multiple applications

text: Single sign-out logs a user out of all applications at once
quote: Keycloak provides single-sign out, which means users only have to logout once to be logged-out of all applications that use Keycloak.

text: Social login can be enabled purely via admin console configuration, no app code changes

text: Exposes health REST endpoints to check startup/readiness status

text: Realms act as isolated multi-tenant boundaries for users and applications
quote: A realm in Keycloak is equivalent to a tenant. Each realm allows an administrator to create isolated groups of applications and users.

text: Admins can centrally manage users, their permissions, and active sessions
quote: They can also manage users, including permissions and sessions.

text: Users can link their account to multiple identity providers for alternate sign-in
quote: If you've enabled social login or identity brokering users can also link their accounts with additional providers to allow them to authenticate to the same account with different identity providers.

text: Provides a token introspection endpoint to validate access or refresh tokens
quote: The introspection endpoint is used to retrieve the active state of a token. In other words, you can use it to validate an access or refresh token.

text: Provides a token revocation endpoint for both access and refresh tokens
quote: The token revocation endpoint is used to revoke tokens. Both refresh tokens and access tokens are supported by this endpoint.
